subject: Request: Preferred access + competitive clause waiver for Avery Systems
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@averysystems.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: purchasing@averysystems.com
Date: 2028-03-21 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Preferred access & competitive preference request for pilot

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Avery is excited about what Redwood can do for our user-facing summarization pipeline. We have one procurement ask that sits a little outside your standard terms: Avery is requesting a 12-month "preferred access" window tied to our pilot. Concretely, we want a commitment that Redwood will provide (a) capacity priority for our reserved pool during our pilot (up to 2x baseline throughput) and (b) a limited non-compete/preference carveout: Redwood would not onboard a direct competitor in our vertical with materially better commercial terms during the 12-month window.

We recognize that MFN-like clauses are sensitive. We're proposing the following to make this workable:
- Preferred access window: 12 months from go-live
- Revenue commitment: $300k TCV for the pilot and initial renewal
- If Redwood offers superior commercial terms to a direct competitor, Avery gets the option to match (no retroactive credits)

Attached is the draft SOW and a one-pager on our expected usage profile. Can your team tell me what level of escalation this requires and whether Redwood can accept something along these lines (or propose mitigations)?

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a 30-min call if easier.

Best,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Partnerships
Avery Systems

Attachments:
- Avery_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW, redlines to follow)
- usage_profile_q1.xlsx

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@averysystems.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-21 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preferred access & competitive preference request for pilot

Liam — thanks for the clarity and the SOW. Great to hear the pilot went well. I've looped in Ben (Legal) and Laura (Deal Desk) to weigh in; flagging up front: MFN / no-onboard commitments are high-risk for us and will need Exec sign-off.

A few quick reactions from product/ops perspective:
- Capacity priority is something we can operationalize with a reserved pool and burst policy, but it needs a clear SLA and a defined revenue floor.
- The "no onboarding of a direct competitor" language is effectively an exclusivity-like restriction and is the part Legal will push back on.

Suggested compromise to propose back to Avery (pending Legal/Exec):
1) Preferred access window: 9 months instead of 12
2) Revenue-triggered priority: priority holds while Avery maintains $250k ARR equivalent in the committed period
3) No broad "no onboard" language — instead, a right of first match for commercial terms for 180 days if we sign a like-for-like competitor in the same vertical; this is limited in scope and duration.

Ben/Laura — could you review the attached redline once you have a moment? If we escalate, I'd like a short memo with recommended guardrails and the minimum approvals needed.

Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

On attachments: I have Avery_SOW_v3.pdf; please add any legal redlines as new attachments and keep the HubSpot deal updated (deal ID RDW-2028-2147).

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-22 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preferred access & competitive preference request for pilot

Team — looked through Liam's ask and Sean's proposed compromise. Legal concerns are: MFN/"no onboard" language creates product gating and market restrictions that expose Redwood to competitive risk and resale obligations. Specific notes: 
- MFN-like clauses can create open-ended repricing liabilities; avoid any retroactive price protection.
- "No onboard" clauses are near-exclusivity; we shouldn't agree to absolute restrictions.

My recommendation: escalate to Exec for one-time exception only if Deal Desk structures a tightly-scoped term sheet with:
A) Fixed duration: 9 months max for preferred access;
B) Revenue floor trigger: $250k TCV minimum;
C) Match-right instead of MFN: Avery has 30 days to match any materially better commercial offer we grant to a like-for-like competitor; no retroactive credits;
D) Competitor definition: explicitly list named competitors or define by product functionality to reduce ambiguity;
E) Cap total committed capacity premium (e.g., up to 2x baseline for pilot and then renegotiate).

I've attached my inline redline (legal_redline_comments.docx) and a short risk memo. If Exec approves, Legal needs a single sign-off and a post-signature monitoring plan (quarterly review) to ensure we don't create precedent.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- legal_redline_comments.docx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-22 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preferred access & competitive preference request for pilot — Deal Desk recommendation

Markus — looping you for Exec consideration. Summary and recommendation below.

Deal summary: Avery Systems (deal RDW-2028-2147) is asking for a 12-month preferred access window and an MFN/preference-style carveout. Pilot TCV is ~$300k; multi-year potential if pilot scales. Primary risk is competitive restriction precedent and pricing exposure.

Deal Desk recommendation (we propose to offer the following, subject to Exec sign-off):
1) Preferred access: 9 months from go-live, operationalized via Dedicated pool with burst up to 2x baseline throughput.
2) Revenue floor: preference remains only while Avery meets $250k committed usage in first 9 months (measured by billings).
3) Match-right (not MFN): if we provide materially better commercial terms to a like-for-like competitor within 180 days, Avery has a 30-day right to elect equivalent terms for future bookings only (no retroactive credits).
4) Competitor carveout: define competitor by product feature set and list the three named vendors we consider direct (A, B, C) to reduce ambiguity.
5) Term cap + monitoring: limited to stated pilot/first-year period and quarterly review; Legal to sign off monitoring cadence.

Attachments: I've included a term matrix (preferred_access_term_matrix.xlsx) and Ben's redline. If you approve, we'll communicate the compromise to Liam and request Avery accept the limited match-right and revenue trigger.

Next steps request for Exec: approval to offer 9-month preferred access with the above guardrails and to let Legal and Deal Desk finalize contractual language. If Exec wants to tighten or loosen duration/revenue floor, please indicate.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-23 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preferred access & competitive preference request for pilot — Exec decision

Team — thanks for the clear summary and mitigation options. I'm comfortable approving a one-time exception under the Deal Desk recommendation with the following conditions: 
1) Preferred access duration capped at 9 months (no extensions without Exec re-approval).
2) Revenue floor set at $275k (midpoint between proposed numbers) measured by committed billings in the first 9 months.
3) Match-right window: 120 days instead of 180; no retroactive credits, and scope limited to "user-facing summarization services" as defined in the SOW.
4) Legal to add a clause that explicitly prohibits Avery from claiming exclusivity in marketing materials and requires a public partner reference if they claim preferential treatment.
5) Deal Desk to add an automatic 60-day implementation review (ops & cost impact) and billing holdback clause in case of measurable SLA misses.

Once Legal finalizes language, Laura/Sean — proceed to communicate to Avery. If Avery pushes back hard on either the duration or revenue floor, bring it back to me.

Markus Klein
VP, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Exec_approval_note.pdf (internal decision memo)
